newsitem.title: UK: Railways fund monitors MGAM, sees no change.
newsitem.headline: Railways fund monitors MGAM, sees no change.

text.p: Britain's Railways Pension Fund, one of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's main clients, said on Tuesday it would be monitoring MGAM's performance after recent events but planned no changes in its relationship with the firm.

"We will be monitoring their actions to see if things carry on despite the changes in personnel but we have no plans to make any changes," said David Adams, chief executive of the Railways Pension Trustee Company. "We have been extremely pleased with their performance, we are very happy with the integrity of the controls of their systems, and we think the current investment process is very impressive."
MGAM clients have been disturbed by recent events which culminated in the acrimonious resignation last week of star fund manager Nicola Horlick.
Most have been extremely impressed by MGAM's performance over the past three to five years though most remain concerned about stability within the firm, looking ahead.
With 1.25 billion pounds invested with MGAM, the Railways Pension Fund is one of MGAM's biggest clients.

On Monday a number of British regional councils, with pension funds under MGAM management, said they were keeping the situation under review due to concerns about future stability, despite an MGAM statement assuring them of the loyalty of Horlicks' team.
But most said they were pleased with MGAM's performance to date.
